Explain why solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity but molten sodium chloride does.
In solid sodium chloride, the ions are held in fixed positions in the lattice
No charge can flow, so no conduction
In molten sodium chloride, the ions are free to move
Na⁺ ions can move to the cathode
Cl⁻ ions can move to the anode
Charge can flow, so conduction occurs
In the electrolysis of molten zinc chloride, state:
a) Which electrode zinc forms at
b) Whether this is oxidation or reduction
a) Zinc ions (Zn²⁺) are positive, so they are attracted to the negative electrode (cathode)
b) At the cathode, Zn²⁺ gains electrons: Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Zn
Write the half-equations for the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride.
Cathode is negative (Cations go there); Anode is positive (Anions go there)
Ions must be free to move - only molten or dissolved compounds work
Getting oxidation and reduction the wrong way round
Reduction at Cathode (RED CAT); Oxidation at Anode (AN OX)
